requests an effective date of January 15, 2026, consistent with the effective date granted in
the January 14 Order.

2.     High Impact Large Load

       2.1    Obtaining Transmission Service for High Impact Large Load

 If the load associated with the delivery point addition or modification is a HILL as defined in
Part I of the Tariff, the Transmission Customer or the Network Customer must satisfy the
requirements outlined in this Attachment BA in addition to the requirements of Attachment AQ
and Attachment AX, as applicable.

              2.1.1   Transmission Customer or Network Customer Has Sufficient
                      Designated Resources for the Requested Transmission Service

                      If the Transmission Provider determines that the Transmission Customer
                      or the Network Customer has sufficient existing Designated Resources to
                      serve its full megawatt amount of existing load and the forecasted
                      megawatt amount of requested transmission service for the HILL,
                      including losses, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer is
                      eligible to proceed with the applicable requirements of Attachment AQ of
                      the Tariff.

              2.1.2   Transmission Customer or Network Customer Does Not Have
                      Sufficient Designated Resources for the Requested Transmission
                      Service

                      If the Transmission Provider determines that the Transmission Customer
                      or the Network Customer does not have sufficient existing Designated
                      Resources to serve its full megawatt amount of existing load and the
                      forecasted megawatt amount of requested service for the HILL, including
                      losses, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer may:

                      (a) Proceed with the requirements of Attachment AQ of the Tariff for any
                          megawatt amounts of requested service of the HILL that can be served
                          by existing Designated Resources; and/or

                      (b) Proceed with the requirements of Attachment AX of the Tariff if the
                          Transmission Customer or Network Customer has planned generation
            for any megawatt amounts of requested transmission service of the
           HILL that cannot be served by existing Designated Resources.

2.1.3   High Impact Large Load Request

        When the Transmission Provider receives a request from a Transmission
        Customer or a Network Customer to modify, retire, replace or establish a
        delivery point under Attachment AQ and/or Attachment AX of the Tariff
        to serve a HILL, the provisions of this Section 2.1.3 apply. For the
        purposes of this Section 2.1.3, Host Transmission Owner is defined as the
        owner of that portion of the Transmission System to which such
        connection or modification is to be made.

        2.1.3.1 Study Requests for Additions of or Changes to a HILL

               The Transmission Customer or Network Customer will make any
               request for changes in delivery facilities, including the
               establishment, retirement, replacement, and modification of any
               HILL delivery point in writing to the Transmission Provider and
               the Host Transmission Owner pursuant to Attachment AQ and
               Attachment AX of the Tariff. Such request must contain as much
               information as is known or projected at the time of the request as
               set forth in Addendum 1 to Attachment AQ and/or Addendum 1 to
               Attachment AX.

        2.1.3.2 Studies

               In addition to the studies required pursuant to Attachment AQ and
               Attachment AX of the Tariff, the Transmission Provider and Host
               Transmission Owner will conduct all necessary studies associated
               with the HILL delivery point. Such additional studies will be
               conducted at the Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
               expense pursuant to the provisions of this section. The requested
               change in HILL delivery point configuration results in the HILL
               supplemental studies as described in Sections 2.1.3.3 and 2.1.3.4 of
       this Attachment BA. Transmission Provider will coordinate the
      supplemental studies necessary to evaluate the HILL.

2.1.3.3 HILL Supplemental Load Connection Study

      Host Transmission Owner must respond within ten (10) Business
      Days of receipt of such request and may provide a HILL
      Supplemental Load Connection Study (“HSLCS”) Agreement for
      any additional information that Host Transmission Owner requires
      from the Transmission Customer or Network Customer to proceed
      with the study of the HILL. Unless otherwise agreed, the HSLCS
      Agreement will commit the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer to pay Host Transmission Owner the actual cost to
      complete the study. The Host Transmission Owner may require an
      advance deposit of $25,000 for the HSLCS, which is in addition to
      the Load Connection Study deposit(s) required in Attachment AQ
      and/or Attachment AX of the Tariff. In conducting any HSLCS,
      the Host Transmission Owner will assess the HILL delivery point
      by using any other additional analyses that may be appropriate.


      If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer fails to return
      an executed HSLCS Agreement, if required, within thirty (30)
      Calendar Days of receipt along with any required deposit, or at a
      later date as the Parties may mutually agree, Host Transmission
      Owner will deem the HILL study request to be withdrawn. The
      Transmission Customer or Network Customer may withdraw the
      HILL request at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to
      Host Transmission Owner and Transmission Provider.            Host
      Transmission Owner must complete any required HSLCS and
      issue a HILL Supplemental Connection Report to the Transmission
      Customer or Network Customer and the Transmission Provider
      within ninety (90) Calendar Days after receipt of an executed
      HSLCS Agreement, any required deposit and any necessary data,
       or at a later date as the Parties may mutually agree.
      Upon completion of the HSLCS, the Transmission Customer or
      Network Customer must reimburse Host Transmission Owner for
      the unpaid cost of any HSLCS if the cost of HSLCS exceeds the
      deposit.     Host Transmission Owner must refund to the
      Transmission Customer or Network Customer any portion of the
      deposit that exceeds the cost of any HSLCS with interest earned in
      the interest-bearing account in which Host Transmission Owner
      has placed the deposit, or if such account does not exist, with
      interest calculated in accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a(a)(2).


2.1.3.4 HILL Delivery Point Study (“HDPS”)

      The   Transmission    Provider   will   perform   a   supplemental
      assessment, in addition to the studies required pursuant to
      Attachment AQ and Attachment AX of the Tariff, of the impact of
      a requested HILL delivery point configuration change on the
      Transmission System for the full requested term, in addition to the
      studies required in Attachment AQ and Attachment AX of the
      Tariff.    For all requested HILL delivery point changes, the
      Transmission Provider will deliver to the Transmission Customer
      or Network Customer a HILL Delivery Point Study (“HDPS”)
      Agreement and a request for any additional information that it
      requires from the Transmission Customer or Network Customer to
      proceed with such supplemental study. The HDPS Agreement will
      commit the Transmission Customer or Network Customer to pay
      the costs outlined in Section 2.1.3.5 of this Attachment BA.

      The Transmission Customer or Network Customer must execute
      and deliver the HDPS Agreement and required deposit to the
      Transmission Provider as soon as reasonably possible, but not later
      than thirty (30) Calendar Days following receipt of the HDPS
 Agreement or at a later date as the Parties may mutually agree.
Upon receipt of the executed HDPS Agreement, the study data,
and the required deposit, Transmission Provider will perform the
HDPS. Through the HDPS, the Transmission Provider will assess
the impacts on the Transmission System caused by modifying,
retiring, or replacing an existing HILL delivery point or
establishing the new HILL delivery point using the appropriate
analyses required in accordance with Southwest Power Pool, Inc.,
Open Access Transmission Tariff Business Practices, Business
Practice 7850 and other applicable criteria or reliability standards.
If the Transmission Provider identifies the need to perform a
detailed Electromagnetic Transient (“EMT”) study, an additional
deposit will be required pursuant Section 2.1.3.5 of this
Attachment BA.

If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer fails to return
an executed HDPS Agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days of
receipt, or at a later date as the Parties may mutually agree,
Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will deem
the study request to be withdrawn. The Transmission Customer or
Network Customer may withdraw its HDPS request at any time by
written notice of such withdrawal to the Transmission Provider and
the Host Transmission Owner.

Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will issue a
study report to the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
and Host Transmission Owner within ninety (90) Calendar Days of
all the Parties agreeing to the study. If the Transmission Provider
is unable to complete the study within ninety (90) Calendar Days,
the Transmission Provider will notify the Transmission Customer
or Network Customer and the Host Transmission Owner and
provide an estimate of the time needed to reach a final
       determination along with an explanation of the reason(s) that
      additional time is required to complete the study.

      For any Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s request
      in a completed HDPS having identified third party impact(s) where
      the Transmission Customer or Network Customer has not reached
      an agreement with the third party in accordance with Part II,
      Section 21 of this Tariff, the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer has until the start date of its requested service for a HILL
      delivery point or one (1) year after the completion of the HDPS,
      whichever is sooner, to complete such negotiations to resolve the
      third party issue(s). The Transmission Provider may grant a 90-
      Calendar dDay extension for completion of such negotiations, at
      the request of the Transmission Customer or Network Customer. If
      an extension is granted, the start date of the requested service will
      be deferred if necessary. If the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer has not notified the Transmission Provider of a
      successful conclusion to the negotiation with the third party by the
      deadline described above, the Transmission Provider will deem the
      service request to be terminated and withdrawn.

      If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer notifies the
      Transmission Provider of the successful conclusion of the
      negotiation with the third party by the deadline described this
      Section 2.1.3.4, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
      may move forward with obtaining service under this Tariff.

2.1.3.5 Study Costs for HDPS

      A Transmission Customer or a Network Customer requesting
      HDPS will be responsible for the additional costs to complete the
      HDPS necessary to evaluate the HILL. The Transmission
      Customer or Network Customer must provide a $10,000 non-
 refundable application fee for the HILL. The application fee, is
initially set at $10,000, to be adjusted in accordance with the
Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers as posted on the
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics website. The inflation adjustment
will be calculated from the original application fee amount of
$10,000, to the most up-to-date data available at the time the
inflation calculation takes place, where such amount will be
rounded to the nearest $100 and posted on the Transmission
Provider’s website. The Transmission Provider will post an
inflation-adjusted application fee once every three years, with the
first posting on or after January 1, 2028. The application fee
amount calculated pursuant to this paragraph will be applicable to
all HILL delivery point requests submitted sixty (60) or more
Calendar Days after the date that the Transmission Provider posts
such amount and will remain effective until Transmission Provider
posts a revised amount pursuant to this paragraph.


Additionally, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must make an advance deposit of $100,000 for the HDPS, which is
in addition to the study deposit(s) required by Attachment AQ and
Attachment AX of the Tariff. If the Transmission Provider
determines the need to perform a detailed EMT analysis, the
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must make an
advance deposit of $200,000, which is in addition to the $100,000
advance deposit required in this section. Upon completion of the
HDPS, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer must
reimburse Transmission Provider for any unpaid costs of the
HDPS if the cost of the study exceeds the total deposit(s).
Transmission Provider must refund the Transmission Customer or
Network Customer, with interest earned in the interest-bearing
                      account in which Transmission Provider placed the deposit, any
                     portion of the deposit that exceeds the cost of the HDPS.

              2.1.3.6 Engineering, Design and Construction of New Facilities

                     The Transmission Customer or Network Customer and Host
                     Transmission Owner will agree to and specify in writing each
                     party’s responsibility for engineering, design, construction, and
                     cost of facilities described in the final HILL Supplemental
                     Connection Report.

2.2   Additional Requirements for High Impact Large Loads

      2.2.1   Transmission Service

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission
              Customer or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to
              Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Open Access Transmission Tariff Business
              Practices, Business Practice 7850, in addition to the data required to be
              provided pursuant to Attachments AQ or Attachment AX of the Tariff.

      2.2.2   Integrated Marketplace

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission
              Customer or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to
              Section 2.2 of Attachment AE of the Tariff and pursuant to the Market
              Protocols.

      2.2.3   Generation Interconnection Process

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission
              Customer or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to
              Attachment BB of the Tariff.

      2.2.4   Additional Requirements for Phasor Measurement Unit (“PMU”)
              Prior to Service Commencement Date of the HILL, phasor measurement
              recording and communications equipment must be installed by the Host
 Transmission Owner at Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
expense that is capable of gathering phasor measurements as specified in
the SPP PMU Communications Handbook. To the extent similar quality
equipment is being added or already exists, such as relays or digital fault
recorders, that can collect data at least at the same rate as PMUs and
which data is synchronized via a high-accuracy satellite clock, such
equipment can be utilized to satisfy this requirement if the equipment is
located on the Host Transmission Owner’s side of the interconnection.
The phasor measurement equipment must be installed at the Host
Transmission Owner’s side of HILL interconnection and become part of
the   Host   Transmission    Owner    interconnection    facilities.   Phasor
measurements must be streamed in Institute of Electrical and Electronics
Engineers (IEEE) C37.118 or equivalent format and be provided to the
Transmission Provider. This data must at least be sufficient to determine
(i) positive-sequence voltage magnitude and angle, (ii) positive-sequence
current magnitude and angle, (iii) frequency, and (iv) rate of change of
frequency. Such data must be transmitted over the data circuit(s) as
described below. Each Party will promptly advise the other Parties if it
detects or otherwise learns of any metering, telemetry or communications
equipment errors or malfunctions that require the attention and/or
correction by the applicable Party. The Party owning such equipment must
correct such error or malfunction as soon as reasonably feasible.


Transmission Customer or Network Customer must maintain satisfactory
operating communications with Transmission Provider or representative
designated by Transmission Provider. Transmission Customer or Network
Customer must provide standard voice line, dedicated voice line and
facsimile communications through use of either the public telephone
system, or a voice communications system that does not rely on the public
telephone system. Transmission Customer or Network Customer must also
provide the dedicated data circuit(s) necessary to provide such customer’s
               data to Transmission Provider. The data circuit(s) must extend from the
              HILL interconnection to the location(s) specified by Transmission
              Provider. Any required maintenance of such communications equipment
              will be performed by Transmission Customer or Network Customer.
              Operational communications must be activated and maintained under, but
              not be limited to, the following events: system paralleling or separation,
              scheduled and unscheduled shutdowns, equipment clearances, and hourly
              and daily load data.


              Infrastructure security of Transmission System equipment and operations
              and control hardware and software are essential to ensure day-to-day
              Transmission System reliability and operational security.


      2.2.5   Ride-Through Requirements

              Prior to Service Commencement Date of the HILL, the Transmission
              Customer or Network Customer must comply with the ride-through
              requirement guidelines outlined in the SPP HILL Ride-Through
              Requirements.


2.3   Data and Information

      A Transmission Customer or Network Customer submitting information or data
      under this Attachment BA must include information, parameters, and limitations
      that reflect the Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s reasonable
      assessment of the characteristics of the HILL and capabilities of the resources and
      transmission facilities. A Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
      reasonable assessment may be informed by environmental and recreational
      limitations, operating constraints, operating permits or licenses, applicable law,
      warranty and other equipment limitations or requirements, actions and
      instructions by applicable government agencies, and Good Utility Practice, among
      other factors.
 Section 1.    Definitions

       Affected System is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Affected System Operator is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Affiliate is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Applicable Laws and Regulations is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Applicable Reliability Standards is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Balancing Authority shall mean the responsible entity that integrates resource plans
ahead of time, maintains load-interchange-generation balance within a Balancing Authority
Area, and supports Interconnection frequency in real time in order to:
       (1) Match, at all times, the power output of the generators within the electric power
              system(s) and capacity and energy purchased from entities outside the electric
              power system(s), with the load within the electric power system(s);
       (2) Maintain scheduled interchange with other Balancing Authority Areas, within the
              limits of Good Utility Practice;
       (3) Maintain the frequency of the electric power system(s) within reasonable limits in
              accordance with Good Utility Practice; and
       (4) Provide for sufficient generating capacity to maintain operating reserves in
              accordance with Good Utility Practice.
       Balancing Authority Area shall mean the collection of generation, transmission, and
loads within the metered boundaries of the Balancing Authority. The Balancing Authority
maintains load-resource balance within this area.
       Base Case is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Breach will mean the failure of a Party to perform or observe any material term or
condition of the HILLGIA.
       Breaching Party will mean a Party that is in Breach of the HILLGIA.
       Business Day is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
       Calendar Day is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
       Commercial Operation is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
     Commercial Operation Date is the date on which the Generating Facility commences
Commercial Operation of a unit as agreed to by the Parties pursuant to Appendix E to the
HILLGIA.
       Confidential Information is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
      Contingent Facilities will mean those unbuilt Interconnection Facilities and Network
Upgrades upon which the Interconnection Request’s costs, timing, and study findings are
dependent, and if delayed or not built, could cause a need for restudies of the Interconnection
 Request or a reassessment of the Interconnection Facilities and/or Network Upgrades and/or
costs and timing. Contingent Facilities are identified in Appendix A of the HILLGIA.
        Default will mean the failure of a Breaching Party to cure its Breach in accordance with
Article 17 of the HILLGIA.
       Definitive Interconnection System Impact Study (DISIS) is as defined in Attachment
V of the Tariff.
          Deliverability Area is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Dispute Resolution will mean the procedure in Section 13.5 of this Attachment BB for
resolution of a dispute between the Parties in which they will first attempt to resolve the dispute
on an informal basis.
          Distribution System is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
          Distribution Upgrades is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Effective Date will mean the date on which the HILLGIA becomes effective upon
execution by the Parties subject to acceptance by FERC, or if filed unexecuted, upon the date
specified by FERC.
      Electric Reliability Organization shall mean the North American Electric Reliability
Corporation (NERC) or its successor organization.
        Electric Storage Resource Load Assessment (ESR-LA) will have the meaning defined
in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
          Electromagnetic Transient Study or EMT Study is as defined in Attachment V of the
Tariff.

        Emergency Condition will mean a condition or situation: (1) that in the judgment of the
Party making the claim is imminently likely to endanger life or property; or (2) that, in the case
of a Transmission Provider, is imminently likely (as determined in a non-discriminatory manner)
to cause a material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to the Transmission System, or
the electric systems of others to which the Transmission Provider's Transmission System is
directly connected; or (3) that, in the case of Transmission Owner, is imminently likely (as
determined in a non-discriminatory manner) to cause a material adverse effect on the security of,
or damage to Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Facilities; or (4) that, in the case of
HILLGA Customer, is imminently likely (as determined in a non-discriminatory manner) to
cause a material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to, the Generating Facility or
HILLGA Customer's Interconnection Facilities. System restoration and black start will be
considered Emergency Conditions; provided that HILLGA Customer is not obligated by the
HILLGIA to possess black start capability.
          Engineering & Procurement (E&P) Agreement is as defined in Attachment V of the
Tariff.
          Environmental Law is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Environmental Review will mean a study conducted by WAPA-Division, as the
Transmission Owner, that contains a review of the proposed interconnection to the WAPA-
Division’s transmission facilities, pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act (“NEPA”),
42 U.S.C. §4321, et seq., as amended, and setting forth HILLGA Customer’s responsibilities in
connection with such review of the interconnection.
       Existing Generating Facility is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Federal Power Act is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       FERC is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Financial Security will mean the security deposits required of the HILLGA Customer to
enter the HILLGA.
       Force Majeure is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generating Facility will mean a HILLGA Customer's device(s) for the production
and/or storage for later injection of electricity identified in the HILLGA Request, but will not
include HILLGA Customer's Interconnection Facilities and will not include a Storage as
Transmission Only Asset as defined in Section 1 of the Tariff. A Generating Facility consists of
one or more generating unit(s) and/or storage device(s) which usually can operate independently
and be brought online or taken offline individually.
       Generating Facility Capacity is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generating Facility Modification is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generator Interconnection Procedures (GIP) will mean the interconnection
procedures applicable to an Interconnection Request pertaining to a Generating Facility that are
included in Attachment V of the Transmission Provider's Tariff.
       Good Utility Practice is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
       Governmental Authority is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Hazardous Substances is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       High Impact Large Load (HILL) is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
         High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment (HILLGA) will mean an
engineering process that evaluates the impact of the proposed interconnection on the safety and
reliability of Transmission System and, if applicable, an Affected System. The HILLGA is part
of HILL processes that study: 1) the proposed load, 2) the proposed Generating Facility to follow
the proposed load, and 3) the combination of the supported proposed load and proposed
Generating Facility to follow the proposed load.
        High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment Customer (HILLGA Customer,
HILLGAC) will mean an Interconnection Customer that proposes to interconnect its Generating
Facility with the Transmission System pursuant to the High Impact Large Load Generation
Assessment.
        High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment Local Interconnection (HILLGA-
Local) will mean a HILL generator connected to the Transmission System in close proximity to
the HILL in accordance with Section 3.1.3(5)a of this Attachment BB.

             Point Study (“HDPS”) Agreement.

             HILLGA Customers may request a level of Load Limited Resource
             Interconnection Service below the full Generating Facility Capacity. These
             requests for Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service will be studied at the
             level of service requested for purposes of the HILL to determine the cost of the
             Interconnection Facilities, Network Upgrades, and associated costs. The generator
             may be subject to other studies at the full Generating Facility Capacity to ensure
             the safety and reliability of the Transmission System, with the study costs borne
             by the HILLGA Customer. If after the additional studies are complete,
             Transmission Provider determines that additional Network Upgrades are
             necessary, then Transmission Provider must: (1) specify which additional
             Network Upgrade costs are based on which studies; and (2) provide a detailed
             explanation of why the additional Network Upgrades are necessary. Any
             Interconnection Facility and/or Network Upgrade costs required for safety and
             reliability would also be borne by the HILLGA Customer. HILLGA Customers
             may be subject to additional control technologies as well as testing and validation
             of those technologies consistent with Article 6 of the HILLGIA. The necessary
             control technologies and protection systems will be established in Appendix C of
             the executed, or requested to be filed unexecuted, HILLGIA.

             electric storage resource at non-peak load and using the operating assumptions
             requested by HILLGA Customer, unless Transmission Provider determines that
             Good Utility Practice, including Applicable Reliability Standards, otherwise
             requires the use of different operating assumptions. Transmission Provider will
             study these requests for Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, with the
             study costs borne by HILLGA Customer, using the submitted operating
             assumptions. These requests for Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service

             Customer. HILLGA Customer’s Generating Facility may be subject to additional
 control technologies as well as testing and validation of additional control

3.8   Identification of Contingent Facilities.

      Contingent Facilities, which may include JTIQ Upgrades, will be identified at the
      conclusion of the HILLGA System Impact Study and included in the HILLGA
      Customer’s HILLGIA. Transmission Provider will also provide, upon request of
      the HILLGA Customer, the estimated Interconnection Facility and/or Network
      Upgrade costs and estimated in-service completion time of each identified
      Contingent Facility when this information is readily available and not
      commercially sensitive.
      Prior to assigning cost allocation for new upgrades pursuant to Section 4.2.2 of
      this Attachment BB, the Transmission Provider will first mitigate constraints seen
 in the study process with Network Upgrades that are part of the current SPP
Transmission Expansion Plan. Network Upgrades that are not yet approved, but
are currently assigned to active prior-queued Interconnection Requests will not be
considered.

For each Network Upgrade identified, the average incremental power flow impact
of each HILLGA Request, as defined in Section 4.2.2 of this Attachment BB, will
be determined using each seasonal model available for the study period during
which the generating facility associated with the HILLGA Request is most likely
to be generating at nameplate capacity, after the Date Upgrade Needed, as defined
in Section 4.2.2 of this Attachment BB, of such upgraded facility. Each impact
amount will be determined by first establishing a set of initial seasonal Base Case
power flow models that excludes flows associated with the HILLGA Request.
Then the HILLGA Request will be added to the models and the change in flow
across such Network Upgrades will be determined. Dependence on a Network
Upgrade will be assigned if the HILLGA Request has a positive incremental
impact on such Network Upgrade with a distribution factor that is greater than or
equal to the amounts set forth in Sections 3.8.1. Incremental flows having a
negative impact (counter flow) on a Network Upgrade will be ignored.

3.8.1   The distribution factor for non-binding NRIS to the Deliverability Area
        (DA) will be 3% for all constraints.
 Section 4.    HILLGA Request Evaluation Process

       Once a HILLGA Customer has submitted a valid HILLGA Request pursuant to Sections
       3.4 and 8.2 of this Attachment BB, such HILLGA Request shall become part of
       Transmission Provider’s interconnection queue for further processing pursuant to the
       following procedures.
       4.1    Priority.

              4.1.1   The Transmission Provider will assign a Queue Position to each HILLGA
                      Request based on the date and time of receipt of the valid HILLGA
                      Request; provided that if the sole reason a HILLGA Request is not valid is
                      the lack of required information on the application form, and HILLGA
                      Customer provides such information in accordance with Section 3.4.3 of
                      the this Attachment BB, then Transmission Provider will assign HILLGA
                      Customer a Queue Position based on the date the application form was
                      originally submitted to the Transmission Provider. The Queue Position of
                      each HILLGA Request will determine the order in which HILLGA
                      Requests are processed.

       4.2    General Study Process.

              4.2.1 HILLGA System Impact Study Procedures.

                      Transmission Provider will accept HILLGA Requests at any time.
                      Following the receipt of the HILLGA Request, there will be a fifteen (15)
                      Calendar Day review period to resolve any deficiencies in the HILLGA
                      Request. Following the HILLGA Request review period, the Transmission
                      Provider will complete the study of the HILLGA Request in accordance
                      with the timeline specified in Section 8.5 of this Attachment BB. The
                      Transmission Provider will study the HILLGA Request separately to the
                      extent warranted by Good Utility Practice.

              4.2.2   Study Cost and Network Upgrade Cost Allocation.

                      The Transmission Provider will determine the cost to the HILLGA
                      Customer. The HILLGA Customer will be responsible to pay for the full
                      cost of the HILLGA Study. If HILLGA Customer withdraws its HILLGA
                      Request before or during the HILLGA Study, the Transmission Provider
                      will stop the study and the HILLGA Customer will be responsible for
                      study costs for the work completed.

                      For Network Upgrades identified in the HILLGA Studies, the
                      Transmission Provider will calculate the cost of Network Upgrade(s). The
                      Transmission Provider will review all Network Upgrades and determine
                      the earliest date that each upgrade is required to be in-service in order to
                      provide the requested Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service
                      (“Date Upgrade Needed”).
 4.3   Transferability of Queue Position.

      A HILLGA Customer may transfer its Queue Position to another entity only if
      such entity acquires the specific Generating Facility identified in the HILLGA
      Request and the Point of Interconnection does not change.

4.4   Modifications.

      HILLGA Customer will submit to Transmission Provider, in writing,
      modifications to any information provided in the HILLGA Request. HILLGA
      Customer will retain its Queue Position if the modifications are in accordance
      with Sections 4.4.1, 4.4.2 or 4.4.5 of this Attachment BB, or are determined not to
      be Material Modifications pursuant to Section 4.4.3 of this Attachment BB. Due
      to the expedited nature of HILLGA, any modification would reset the HILLGA
      System Impact Study’s ninety (90) Calendar Day timing.

      Notwithstanding the above, during the course of the HILLGA System Impact
      Study, either HILLGA Customer or Transmission Provider may propose changes
      to the planned interconnection that may improve the costs and benefits (including
      reliability) of the interconnection, and the ability of the proposed change to
      accommodate the HILLGA Request. To the extent the identified changes are
      acceptable to Transmission Provider and HILLGA Customer, such acceptance not
      to be unreasonably withheld, Transmission Provider will modify the Point of
      Interconnection prior to the end of the HILLGA Review Period and HILLGA
      Customer will retain its Queue Position.

      4.4.1   During HILLGA System Impact Study, modifications to the HILLGA
              Request permitted under this section will include specifically a decrease of
              Maximum Injection Capability and/or Network Resource Deliverability
              (MW) of up to ten percent (10%) of the original requested Maximum
              Injection Capability or Network Resource Deliverability. For increases in
              Nameplate Capacity, Maximum Injection Capability, or Network
              Resource Deliverability, the incremental increase in any of these quantities
              will go to the end of the queue for the purposes of cost allocation and
              study analysis.

      4.4.2   Prior to making any modification other than those specifically permitted
              by Sections 4.4.1, 4.4.4, and 4.4.5 of this Attachment BB, HILLGA
              Customer may first request that Transmission Provider evaluate whether
              such modification is a Material Modification. In response to HILLGA
              Customer's request, Transmission Provider will evaluate the proposed
              modifications prior to making them and inform HILLGA Customer in
              writing of whether the modifications would constitute a Material
              Modification. Any change to the Point of Interconnection, except those
              deemed acceptable under Sections 4.4.1and 8.2 of this Attachment BB or
              so allowed elsewhere, will constitute a Material Modification. HILLGA
         Customer may then withdraw the proposed modification or proceed with a
        new HILLGA Request for such modification.

        Transmission Provider will study the addition of a Generating Facility that
        includes at least one electric storage resource at non-peak load and using
        the operating assumptions requested by HILLGA Customer, unless
        Transmission Provider determines that Good Utility Practice, including
        Applicable Reliability Standards, otherwise requires the use of different
        operating assumptions.

4.4.3   Upon receipt of HILLGA Customer's request for modification permitted
        under this Section 4.4 of this Attachment BB, the Transmission Provider
        will notify the HILLGA Customer if a study is necessary to determine
        whether the change is considered a Material Modification, as defined in
        Attachment V of the Tariff.

4.4.4   Extensions of less than three (3) cumulative years in the Commercial
        Operation Date of the Generating Facility to which the HILLGA Request
        relates are not material and should be handled through construction
        sequencing. For purposes of this section, the Commercial Operation Date
        reflected in the initial HILLGA Request shall be used to calculate the
        permissible extension prior to HILLGA Customer executing a HILLGIA
        or requesting that the HILLGIA be filed unexecuted. After a HILLGIA is
        executed or requested to be filed unexecuted, the Commercial Operation
        Date reflected in the HILLGIA shall be used to calculate the permissible
        extension. Such cumulative extensions may not exceed three years
        including both extensions requested after execution of the HILLGIA by
        HILLGA Customer or the filing of an unexecuted HILLGIA by
        Transmission Provider and those requested prior to execution of the
        HILLGIA by HILLGA Customer or the filing of an unexecuted HILLGIA
        by Transmission Provider. Extensions of more than three (3) cumulative
        years of the Commercial Operation Date of the Generating Facility are
        deemed to be a Material Modification. Extensions of Commercial
        Operation Date due to circumstances in Section 8.7 of this Attachment BB
        are applicable to this Section 4.4.4.

4.4.5   Technological Change Procedure.

        If a HILLGA Customer seeks to incorporate a technological advancement
        into its Generating Facility, it should submit a technological advancement
        request to the Transmission Provider in writing prior to the end of
        HILLGA System Impact Study.

        The technological advancement request must include a description of the
        proposed advancement and provide details necessary to evaluate whether
        the proposed advancement is material, including but not limited to, listing
        the specific parameters in Attachments A and B to Appendix 3 of this
 Attachment BB that would change as a result of the proposed
advancement.

If the proposed technological advancement is a Permissible Technological
Advancement or would not change any of the parameters in Attachments
A or B to Appendix 3 of this Attachment BB, no study will be necessary
and the proposed advancement will not be considered a Material
Modification.

The Transmission Provider will evaluate the request pursuant to Section
4.4.3 of this Attachment BB. Studies conducted for purposes of this
Section 4.4.5 of this Attachment BB will be completed in thirty (30)
Calendar Days after the HILLGA Customer submits a formal
technological advancement request to the transmission provider, provided
that the HILLGA Customer has provided the required information and
study deposit.

2.     High Impact Large Load

       2.1     Obtaining Transmission Service for High Impact Large Load

 If the load associated with the delivery point addition or modification is a HILL as defined in Part
I of the Tariff, the Transmission Customer or the Network Customer must satisfy the requirements
outlined in this Attachment BA in addition to the requirements of Attachment AQ and Attachment
AX, as applicable.

               2.1.1   Transmission Customer or Network Customer Has Sufficient
                       Designated Resources for the Requested Transmission Service

                       If the Transmission Provider determines that the Transmission Customer or
                       the Network Customer has sufficient existing Designated Resources to
                       serve its full megawatt amount of existing load and the forecasted megawatt
                       amount of requested transmission service for the HILL, including losses,
                       the Transmission Customer or Network Customer is eligible to proceed with
                       the applicable requirements of Attachment AQ of the Tariff.

               2.1.2   Transmission Customer or Network Customer Does Not Have
                       Sufficient Designated Resources for the Requested Transmission
                       Service

                       If the Transmission Provider determines that the Transmission Customer or
                       the Network Customer does not have sufficient existing Designated
                       Resources to serve its full megawatt amount of existing load and the
                       forecasted megawatt amount of requested service for the HILL, including
                       losses, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer may:

                       (a) Proceed with the requirements of Attachment AQ of the Tariff for any
                          megawatt amounts of requested service of the HILL that can be served
                          by existing Designated Resources; and/or

                       (b) Proceed with the requirements of Attachment AX of the Tariff if the
                          Transmission Customer or Network Customer has planned generation
            for any megawatt amounts of requested transmission service of the
           HILL that cannot be served by existing Designated Resources.

2.1.3   High Impact Large Load Request

        When the Transmission Provider receives a request from a Transmission
        Customer or a Network Customer to modify, retire, replace or establish a
        delivery point under Attachment AQ and/or Attachment AX of the Tariff to
        serve a HILL, the provisions of this Section 2.1.3 apply. For the purposes
        of this Section 2.1.3, Host Transmission Owner is defined as the owner of
        that portion of the Transmission System to which such connection or
        modification is to be made.

        2.1.3.1 Study Requests for Additions of or Changes to a HILL

               The Transmission Customer or Network Customer will make any
               request for changes in delivery facilities, including the
               establishment, retirement, replacement, and modification of any
               HILL delivery point in writing to the Transmission Provider and the
               Host Transmission Owner pursuant to Attachment AQ and
               Attachment AX of the Tariff. Such request must contain as much
               information as is known or projected at the time of the request as set
               forth in Addendum 1 to Attachment AQ and/or Addendum 1 to
               Attachment AX.

        2.1.3.2 Studies

               In addition to the studies required pursuant to Attachment AQ and
               Attachment AX of the Tariff, the Transmission Provider and Host
               Transmission Owner will conduct all necessary studies associated
               with the HILL delivery point. Such additional studies will be
               conducted at the Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
               expense pursuant to the provisions of this section. The requested
               change in HILL delivery point configuration results in the HILL
               supplemental studies as described in Sections 2.1.3.3 and 2.1.3.4 of
       this Attachment BA. Transmission Provider will coordinate the
      supplemental studies necessary to evaluate the HILL.

2.1.3.3 HILL Supplemental Load Connection Study

      Host Transmission Owner must respond within ten (10) Business
      Days of receipt of such request and may provide a HILL
      Supplemental Load Connection Study (“HSLCS”) Agreement for
      any additional information that Host Transmission Owner requires
      from the Transmission Customer or Network Customer to proceed
      with the study of the HILL. Unless otherwise agreed, the HSLCS
      Agreement will commit the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer to pay Host Transmission Owner the actual cost to
      complete the study. The Host Transmission Owner may require an
      advance deposit of $25,000 for the HSLCS, which is in addition to
      the Load Connection Study deposit(s) required in Attachment AQ
      and/or Attachment AX of the Tariff. In conducting any HSLCS, the
      Host Transmission Owner will assess the HILL delivery point by
      using any other additional analyses that may be appropriate.


      If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer fails to return
      an executed HSLCS Agreement, if required, within thirty (30)
      Calendar Days of receipt along with any required deposit, or at a
      later date as the Parties may mutually agree, Host Transmission
      Owner will deem the HILL study request to be withdrawn. The
      Transmission Customer or Network Customer may withdraw the
      HILL request at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to
      Host Transmission Owner and Transmission Provider.             Host
      Transmission Owner must complete any required HSLCS and issue
      a HILL Supplemental Connection Report to the Transmission
      Customer or Network Customer and the Transmission Provider
      within ninety (90) Calendar Days after receipt of an executed
      HSLCS Agreement, any required deposit and any necessary data, or
       at   a   later   date   as   the   Parties   may    mutually    agree.
      Upon completion of the HSLCS, the Transmission Customer or
      Network Customer must reimburse Host Transmission Owner for
      the unpaid cost of any HSLCS if the cost of HSLCS exceeds the
      deposit. Host Transmission Owner must refund to the Transmission
      Customer or Network Customer any portion of the deposit that
      exceeds the cost of any HSLCS with interest earned in the interest-
      bearing account in which Host Transmission Owner has placed the
      deposit, or if such account does not exist, with interest calculated in
      accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a(a)(2).


2.1.3.4 HILL Delivery Point Study (“HDPS”)

      The Transmission Provider will perform a supplemental assessment,
      in addition to the studies required pursuant to Attachment AQ and
      Attachment AX of the Tariff, of the impact of a requested HILL
      delivery point configuration change on the Transmission System for
      the full requested term. For all requested HILL delivery point
      changes, the Transmission Provider will deliver to the Transmission
      Customer or Network Customer a HILL Delivery Point Study
      (“HDPS”) Agreement and a request for any additional information
      that it requires from the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer to proceed with such supplemental study. The HDPS
      Agreement will commit the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer to pay the costs outlined in Section 2.1.3.5 of this
      Attachment BA.

      The Transmission Customer or Network Customer must execute and
      deliver the HDPS Agreement and required deposit to the
      Transmission Provider as soon as reasonably possible, but not later
      than thirty (30) Calendar Days following receipt of the HDPS
      Agreement or at a later date as the Parties may mutually agree.
 Upon receipt of the executed HDPS Agreement, the study data, and
the required deposit, Transmission Provider will perform the HDPS.
Through the HDPS, the Transmission Provider will assess the
impacts on the Transmission System caused by modifying, retiring,
or replacing an existing HILL delivery point or establishing the new
HILL delivery point using the appropriate analyses required in
accordance with Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Open Access
Transmission Tariff Business Practices, Business Practice 7850 and
other applicable criteria or reliability standards. If the Transmission
Provider identifies the need to perform a detailed Electromagnetic
Transient (“EMT”) study, an additional deposit will be required
pursuant Section 2.1.3.5 of this Attachment BA.

If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer fails to return
an executed HDPS Agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days of
receipt, or at a later date as the Parties may mutually agree,
Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will deem the
study request to be withdrawn. The Transmission Customer or
Network Customer may withdraw its HDPS request at any time by
written notice of such withdrawal to the Transmission Provider and
the Host Transmission Owner.

Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will issue a
study report to the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
and Host Transmission Owner within ninety (90) Calendar Days of
all the Parties agreeing to the study. If the Transmission Provider is
unable to complete the study within ninety (90) Calendar Days, the
Transmission Provider will notify the Transmission Customer or
Network Customer and the Host Transmission Owner and provide
an estimate of the time needed to reach a final determination along
with an explanation of the reason(s) that additional time is required
to complete the study.
       For any Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s request
      in a completed HDPS having identified third party impact(s) where
      the Transmission Customer or Network Customer has not reached
      an agreement with the third party in accordance with Part II,
      Section 21 of this Tariff, the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer has until the start date of its requested service for a HILL
      delivery point or one (1) year after the completion of the HDPS,
      whichever is sooner, to complete such negotiations to resolve the
      third party issue(s). The Transmission Provider may grant a 90-
      Calendar Day extension for completion of such negotiations, at the
      request of the Transmission Customer or Network Customer. If an
      extension is granted, the start date of the requested service will be
      deferred if necessary. If the Transmission Customer or Network
      Customer has not notified the Transmission Provider of a successful
      conclusion to the negotiation with the third party by the deadline
      described above, the Transmission Provider will deem the service
      request to be terminated and withdrawn.

      If the Transmission Customer or Network Customer notifies the
      Transmission Provider of the successful conclusion of the
      negotiation with the third party by the deadline described this
      Section 2.1.3.4, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
      may move forward with obtaining service under this Tariff.

2.1.3.5 Study Costs for HDPS

      A Transmission Customer or a Network Customer requesting HDPS
      will be responsible for the additional costs to complete the HDPS
      necessary to evaluate the HILL. The Transmission Customer or
      Network Customer must provide a $10,000 non-refundable
      application fee for the HILL. The application fee, is initially set at
      $10,000, to be adjusted in accordance with the Consumer Price
      Index for All Urban Consumers as posted on the U.S. Bureau of
 Labor Statistics website. The inflation adjustment will be calculated
from the original application fee amount of $10,000, to the most up-
to-date data available at the time the inflation calculation takes
place, where such amount will be rounded to the nearest $100 and
posted on the Transmission Provider’s website. The Transmission
Provider will post an inflation-adjusted application fee once every
three years, with the first posting on or after January 1, 2028. The
application fee amount calculated pursuant to this paragraph will be
applicable to all HILL delivery point requests submitted sixty (60)
or more Calendar Days after the date that the Transmission Provider
posts such amount and will remain effective until Transmission
Provider posts a revised amount pursuant to this paragraph.


Additionally, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must make an advance deposit of $100,000 for the HDPS, which is
in addition to the study deposit(s) required by Attachment AQ and
Attachment AX of the Tariff. If the Transmission Provider
determines the need to perform a detailed EMT analysis, the
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must make an
advance deposit of $200,000, which is in addition to the $100,000
advance deposit required in this section. Upon completion of the
HDPS, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer must
reimburse Transmission Provider for any unpaid costs of the HDPS
if the cost of the study exceeds the total deposit(s). Transmission
Provider must refund the Transmission Customer or Network
Customer, with interest earned in the interest-bearing account in
which Transmission Provider placed the deposit, any portion of the
deposit that exceeds the cost of the HDPS.
               2.1.3.6 Engineering, Design and Construction of New Facilities

                     The Transmission Customer or Network Customer and Host
                     Transmission Owner will agree to and specify in writing each
                     party’s responsibility for engineering, design, construction, and cost
                     of facilities described in the final HILL Supplemental Connection
                     Report.

2.2   Additional Requirements for High Impact Large Loads

      2.2.1   Transmission Service

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission Customer
              or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to Southwest
              Power Pool, Inc., Open Access Transmission Tariff Business Practices,
              Business Practice 7850, in addition to the data required to be provided
              pursuant to Attachments AQ or Attachment AX of the Tariff.

      2.2.2   Integrated Marketplace

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission Customer
              or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to Section 2.2 of
              Attachment AE of the Tariff and pursuant to the Market Protocols.

      2.2.3   Generation Interconnection Process

              For the study of transmission service to a HILL, the Transmission Customer
              or Network Customer is required to provide data pursuant to Attachment
              BB of the Tariff.

      2.2.4   Additional Requirements for Phasor Measurement Unit (“PMU”)
              Prior to Service Commencement Date of the HILL, phasor measurement
              recording and communications equipment must be installed by the Host
              Transmission Owner at Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
              expense that is capable of gathering phasor measurements as specified in
              the SPP PMU Communications Handbook. To the extent similar quality
 equipment is being added or already exists, such as relays or digital fault
recorders, that can collect data at least at the same rate as PMUs and which
data is synchronized via a high-accuracy satellite clock, such equipment can
be utilized to satisfy this requirement if the equipment is located on the Host
Transmission Owner’s side of the interconnection. The phasor
measurement equipment must be installed at the Host Transmission
Owner’s side of HILL interconnection and become part of the Host
Transmission Owner interconnection facilities. Phasor measurements must
be streamed in Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
C37.118 or equivalent format and be provided to the Transmission Provider.
This data must at least be sufficient to determine (i) positive-sequence
voltage magnitude and angle, (ii) positive-sequence current magnitude and
angle, (iii) frequency, and (iv) rate of change of frequency. Such data must
be transmitted over the data circuit(s) as described below. Each Party will
promptly advise the other Parties if it detects or otherwise learns of any
metering, telemetry or communications equipment errors or malfunctions
that require the attention and/or correction by the applicable Party. The
Party owning such equipment must correct such error or malfunction as
soon as reasonably feasible.


Transmission Customer or Network Customer must maintain satisfactory
operating communications with Transmission Provider or representative
designated by Transmission Provider. Transmission Customer or Network
Customer must provide standard voice line, dedicated voice line and
facsimile communications through use of either the public telephone
system, or a voice communications system that does not rely on the public
telephone system. Transmission Customer or Network Customer must also
provide the dedicated data circuit(s) necessary to provide such customer’s
data to Transmission Provider. The data circuit(s) must extend from the
HILL interconnection to the location(s) specified by Transmission Provider.
Any required maintenance of such communications equipment will be
               performed by Transmission Customer or Network Customer. Operational
              communications must be activated and maintained under, but not be limited
              to, the following events: system paralleling or separation, scheduled and
              unscheduled shutdowns, equipment clearances, and hourly and daily load
              data.


              Infrastructure security of Transmission System equipment and operations
              and control hardware and software are essential to ensure day-to-day
              Transmission System reliability and operational security.


      2.2.5   Ride-Through Requirements

              Prior to Service Commencement Date of the HILL, the Transmission
              Customer or Network Customer must comply with the ride-through
              requirement guidelines outlined in the SPP HILL Ride-Through
              Requirements.


2.3   Data and Information

      A Transmission Customer or Network Customer submitting information or data
      under this Attachment BA must include information, parameters, and limitations
      that reflect the Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s reasonable
      assessment of the characteristics of the HILL and capabilities of the resources and
      transmission facilities. A Transmission Customer’s or Network Customer’s
      reasonable assessment may be informed by environmental and recreational
      limitations, operating constraints, operating permits or licenses, applicable law,
      warranty and other equipment limitations or requirements, actions and instructions
      by applicable government agencies, and Good Utility Practice, among other factors.
 Section 1.     Definitions

       Affected System is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Affected System Operator is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Affiliate is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Applicable Laws and Regulations is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Applicable Reliability Standards is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Balancing Authority shall mean the responsible entity that integrates resource plans ahead
of time, maintains load-interchange-generation balance within a Balancing Authority Area, and
supports Interconnection frequency in real time in order to:
       (1) Match, at all times, the power output of the generators within the electric power
               system(s) and capacity and energy purchased from entities outside the electric
               power system(s), with the load within the electric power system(s);
       (2) Maintain scheduled interchange with other Balancing Authority Areas, within the limits
               of Good Utility Practice;
       (3) Maintain the frequency of the electric power system(s) within reasonable limits in
               accordance with Good Utility Practice; and
       (4) Provide for sufficient generating capacity to maintain operating reserves in accordance
               with Good Utility Practice.
       Balancing Authority Area shall mean the collection of generation, transmission, and
loads within the metered boundaries of the Balancing Authority. The Balancing Authority
maintains load-resource balance within this area.
       Base Case is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Breach will mean the failure of a Party to perform or observe any material term or
condition of the HILLGIA.
       Breaching Party will mean a Party that is in Breach of the HILLGIA.
       Business Day is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
       Calendar Day is as defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
       Commercial Operation is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
     Commercial Operation Date is the date on which the Generating Facility commences
Commercial Operation of a unit as agreed to by the Parties pursuant to Appendix E to the
HILLGIA.
       Confidential Information is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
      Contingent Facilities will mean those unbuilt Interconnection Facilities and Network
Upgrades upon which the Interconnection Request’s costs, timing, and study findings are
dependent, and if delayed or not built, could cause a need for restudies of the Interconnection
 Request or a reassessment of the Interconnection Facilities and/or Network Upgrades and/or costs
and timing. Contingent Facilities are identified in Appendix A of the HILLGIA.
        Default will mean the failure of a Breaching Party to cure its Breach in accordance with
Article 17 of the HILLGIA.
        Definitive Interconnection System Impact Study (DISIS) is as defined in Attachment V
of the Tariff.
          Deliverability Area is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Dispute Resolution will mean the procedure in Section 13.5 of this Attachment BB for
resolution of a dispute between the Parties in which they will first attempt to resolve the dispute
on an informal basis.
          Distribution System is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
          Distribution Upgrades is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Effective Date will mean the date on which the HILLGIA becomes effective upon
execution by the Parties subject to acceptance by FERC, or if filed unexecuted, upon the date
specified by FERC.
      Electric Reliability Organization shall mean the North American Electric Reliability
Corporation (NERC) or its successor organization.
        Electric Storage Resource Load Assessment (ESR-LA) will have the meaning defined
in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.
          Electromagnetic Transient Study or EMT Study is as defined in Attachment V of the
Tariff.

        Emergency Condition will mean a condition or situation: (1) that in the judgment of the
Party making the claim is imminently likely to endanger life or property; or (2) that, in the case of
a Transmission Provider, is imminently likely (as determined in a non-discriminatory manner) to
cause a material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to the Transmission System, or the
electric systems of others to which the Transmission Provider's Transmission System is directly
connected; or (3) that, in the case of Transmission Owner, is imminently likely (as determined in
a non-discriminatory manner) to cause a material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to
Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Facilities; or (4) that, in the case of HILLGA Customer, is
imminently likely (as determined in a non-discriminatory manner) to cause a material adverse
effect on the security of, or damage to, the Generating Facility or HILLGA Customer's
Interconnection Facilities. System restoration and black start will be considered Emergency
Conditions; provided that HILLGA Customer is not obligated by the HILLGIA to possess black
start capability.
          Engineering & Procurement (E&P) Agreement is as defined in Attachment V of the
Tariff.
          Environmental Law is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Environmental Review will mean a study conducted by WAPA-Division, as the
Transmission Owner, that contains a review of the proposed interconnection to the WAPA-
Division’s transmission facilities, pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act (“NEPA”),
42 U.S.C. §4321, et seq., as amended, and setting forth HILLGA Customer’s responsibilities in
connection with such review of the interconnection.
       Existing Generating Facility is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Federal Power Act is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       FERC is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
        Financial Security will mean the security deposits required of the HILLGA Customer to
enter the HILLGA.
       Force Majeure is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generating Facility will mean a HILLGA Customer's device(s) for the production and/or
storage for later injection of electricity identified in the HILLGA Request, but will not include
HILLGA Customer's Interconnection Facilities and will not include a Storage as Transmission
Only Asset as defined in Section 1 of the Tariff. A Generating Facility consists of one or more
generating unit(s) and/or storage device(s) which usually can operate independently and be
brought online or taken offline individually.
       Generating Facility Capacity is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generating Facility Modification is as defined in Attachment V of the Tariff.
       Generator Interconnection Procedures (GIP) will mean the interconnection procedures
applicable to an Interconnection Request pertaining to a Generating Facility that are included in

 Section 3.   HILLGA Requests

       3.1   HILLGA Requests.

             3.1.1   Study Deposits.
             A HILLGA Customer must submit to Transmission Provider a HILLGA Request
             by providing an executed HILLGA Study Agreement in the form of Appendix 1 to
             this Attachment BB, a nonrefundable application fee of $20,000, a study deposit,
             and all other items set forth in Section 8.2 of this Attachment BB. All HILLGA
             Requests must be submitted in the manner specified in Section 1 of the “Guidelines
             for the SPP GIP Process and Business Practices” manual posted on the
             Transmission Provider’s Generator Interconnection Study posting page on OASIS,
             and must be associated with a corresponding executed HILL Delivery Point Study
             (“HDPS”) Agreement.
             3.1.2   Submission.
             HILLGA Customers may request a level of Load Limited Resource Interconnection
             Service below the full Generating Facility Capacity. These requests for Load
             Limited Resource Interconnection Service will be studied at the level of service
             requested for purposes of the HILL to determine the cost of the Interconnection
             Facilities, Network Upgrades, and associated costs. The generator may be subject
             to other studies at the full Generating Facility Capacity to ensure the safety and
             reliability of the Transmission System, with the study costs borne by the HILLGA
             Customer. If after the additional studies are complete, Transmission Provider
             determines that additional Network Upgrades are necessary, then Transmission
             Provider must: (1) specify which additional Network Upgrade costs are based on
             which studies; and (2) provide a detailed explanation of why the additional Network
             Upgrades are necessary. Any Interconnection Facility and/or Network Upgrade
             costs required for safety and reliability would also be borne by the HILLGA
             Customer. HILLGA Customers may be subject to additional control technologies
             as well as testing and validation of those technologies consistent with Article 6 of
             the HILLGIA. The necessary control technologies and protection systems will be
             established in Appendix C of the executed, or requested to be filed unexecuted,
             HILLGIA.
             Transmission Provider will study Generating Facilities that include at least one
             electric storage resource at non-peak load and using the operating assumptions
             requested by HILLGA Customer, unless Transmission Provider determines that
             Good Utility Practice, including Applicable Reliability Standards, otherwise
             requires the use of different operating assumptions. Transmission Provider will
             study these requests for Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, with the
             study costs borne by HILLGA Customer, using the submitted operating
             assumptions. These requests for Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service
             also may be subject to other studies at the full Generating Facility Capacity to
             ensure safety and reliability of the system, with the study costs borne by HILLGA
             Customer. HILLGA Customer’s Generating Facility may be subject to additional
 control technologies as well as testing and validation of additional control
technologies consistent with Article 6 of the HILLGIA. The necessary control
technologies and protection systems will be set forth in Appendix C of HILLGA
Customer’s HILLGIA.
3.1.3        HILLGA Requirements.

HILLGA Customer must meet the following requirements:
 1)     The HILLGA Customer submits the HILLGA Request.
 2)     The projected capacity accreditation MW value, as determined pursuant to
        Attachment AA of the Tariff, for the Generating Facility(ies) submitted in
        the HILLGA Request(s) must not exceed the requested MW load amount
        of the associated HILL Request as specified in the executed HILLGA Study
        Agreement subject to Attachments AQ, AX, or BA of the Tariff, multiplied
        by the max of (a) 110% plus the highest approved Planning Reserve Margin
        percentage effective at time of the HILLGA Study Agreement and set forth
        in the SPP Planning Criteria; or (b) 125%. The calculation is as follows:
        Total capacity of Generating Facility(ies) in HILLGA Request(s) for a
        specified HILL ≤ HILL Request load × Max (110%+PRM ,125%)

 3)     HILLGA Customer must submit a separate HILLGA Request for each
        Generating Facility associated with the HILL. HILLGA Customer must
        provide a Point of Interconnection for each HILLGA Request. Each
        HILLGA Request must be submitted with the correct deposit.
 4)     A HILLGA Request interconnecting to facilities not under SPP’s functional
        control must follow the procedures for non-jurisdictional generator
        interconnections in Section 6.3 of SPP Business Practice 7250.
 5)     The proposed Point of Interconnection for a HILLGA Request connecting
        to the SPP Transmission System must be identified by the HILLGA
        Customer as being in the same local area as the HILL.
        a.      LOCAL INTERCONNECTION: The Point of Interconnection is on
                the Transmission System no more than two substations away from
                the HILL(s) local delivery facilities . A Generating Facility may
                support multiple HILLs if no more than five (5) substations and no
                more than two (2) existing transmission line segments are utilized.
                i.     A Generating Facility connecting to 765 kV transmission is
                       limited to one bus distance to be considered local.
                ii.    The Generating Facility must be capable of following a
                       dispatch signal. It must be able to achieve a ramp rate greater
                       than or equal to the HILL maximum rate as specified in the
                              Market Protocols. It must also be able to maintain this ramp
                             rate for a sufficient duration to ramp to at least 50% of the
                             MW in the HILL’s transmission service.
       6)     Any expected environmental restrictions (e.g. run-time restrictions) or any
              other restrictions or limitations.
      3.1.4   Joint HILLGA Interconnection Requests.
              More than one HILL may be evaluated simultaneously with one or more
              HILLGA Requests. All requested load and generation information for each
              site must be submitted simultaneously with the HILLGA Request.
